requirement_descriptions.PRJ-001: Threat Modeler SHALL ingest tabular interface data (CSV or Excel) describing interfaces between subsystems, components, and functions, and narrative documents (text or structured format) describing the system, its subsystems, components, and functions, in a single analysis run.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-002: Threat Modeler SHALL produce a canonical threat-model graph as the authoritative run artifact.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-003: Threat Modeler SHALL execute a deterministic multi-agent pipeline with auditable stage boundaries.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-004: Threat Modeler SHALL validate every stage output against a defined schema before downstream processing.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-005: Threat Modeler SHALL perform trust-boundary analysis, STRIDE scoring, threat generation, mitigation mapping, STIX packaging, diagram generation, and report generation for each completed run.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-006: Threat Modeler SHALL support human-in-the-loop approval, edit, and override gates at defined decision points.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-007: Threat Modeler SHALL maintain immutable run history with who, what, when, and why metadata for all analyst edits.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-008: Threat Modeler SHALL support configurable model-provider selection through configuration without source-code changes.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-009: Threat Modeler SHALL allow deployment in offline-only mode and policy-approved hybrid mode.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-010: Threat Modeler SHALL provide retrieval-augmented evidence references for generated threats and mitigations when knowledge bases are enabled.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-011: Threat Modeler SHALL produce exportable outputs for canonical JSON, STIX 2.1, Mermaid diagrams, and final markdown report.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-012: Threat Modeler SHALL enforce role-based permissions for author, reviewer, and approver actions.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-013: Threat Modeler SHALL support incremental model enrichment without destructive overwrite of previously approved data.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-014: Threat Modeler SHALL provide selective re-run from an analyst-selected stage after approved edits.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-015: Threat Modeler SHALL fail safely by halting downstream execution when critical validation errors are detected.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-016: Threat Modeler SHALL provide a graphical user interface for all analyst-facing interactions including system input entry, HITL gate review, pipeline status monitoring, stage result review, and output export.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-017: Threat Modeler SHALL support export and import of complete run state snapshots that capture inputs, all intermediate stage results, HITL decisions, prompt configuration, and run metadata.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-018: Threat Modeler SHALL allow authorized users to view, edit, save, and revert each agent prompt through a GUI without requiring source code changes, and SHALL maintain a version history of saved prompt configurations.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-019: Threat Modeler SHALL maintain authoritative runtime execution and provider state in a backend asynchronous state service, and GUI screens SHALL consume this state as read projections rather than owning the runtime source of truth.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-020: When configured for live LLM mode, Threat Modeler SHALL detect any fallback to offline fixture/static execution and SHALL halt execution in a failed state with explicit error details.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-021: Threat Modeler SHALL maintain an explicit semantic version for each major component (agents, orchestrator, HITL service, UI module groups, and export services), and release candidate approval SHALL require a versioned component manifest included in release artifacts.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-022: Threat Modeler SHALL maintain deterministic per-file version identifiers for all component-owned source files, and each release candidate SHALL include a file-level version inventory mapped to component versions.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-023: Threat Modeler SHALL provide and support a LangGraph StateGraph runtime path for multi-stage pipeline routing, while preserving validation and HITL gate semantics. Release validation profiles SHALL execute with `execution_mode=langgraph-compatible`.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-024: Threat Modeler SHALL provide an automated visible-browser validation workflow that uploads CAV fixture files (ICD plus markdown narratives) through the Input Entry UI and verifies files are loaded into the run input workflow.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-025: Threat Modeler SHALL provide an operational web/API runtime that does not require Streamlit, and SHALL reserve Streamlit usage for automated browser-validation workflows only.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-026: Threat Modeler SHALL pass approved outputs between agents through canonical handoff records that preserve stage output version, correlation identifier, and compliance metadata, and SHALL not alter approved content except through an explicit analyst or validation decision.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-027: Threat Modeler SHALL validate ICD spreadsheet input and narrative source documents for required structure, source provenance, and cross-reference consistency before downstream agent handoff, and SHALL surface non-compliance as a structured validation failure or HITL gate condition.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-028: Threat Modeler SHALL have the orchestrator pause execution at HITL gates, persist the gate decision state and rationale, block downstream processing until an approved decision is recorded, and resume from the correct checkpoint only after acceptance.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-029: Threat Modeler SHALL monitor live LLM execution for backend heartbeat staleness and SHALL halt the run in a failed state before the UI timeout elapses when liveness is lost, with an actionable error message.
requirement_descriptions.PRJ-030: Threat Modeler SHALL treat the backend prompt store as the authoritative source for agent prompt configuration and SHALL not silently fall back to file defaults when prompt loading fails; prompt persistence and retrieval errors SHALL be surfaced explicitly.
requirement_descriptions.INT-001: Parser Interface SHALL accept normalized text payloads and table payloads in structured request format.
requirement_descriptions.INT-002: Agent Input Interface SHALL receive canonical graph payload, run metadata, and stage context for each invocation.
requirement_descriptions.INT-003: Agent Output Interface SHALL return canonical graph payload and stage result status in a schema-valid structure.
requirement_descriptions.INT-004: Validation Interface SHALL return pass or fail result with machine-readable error codes and locations.
requirement_descriptions.INT-005: Orchestrator Interface SHALL expose stage transition events with stage name, timestamp, and correlation identifier.
requirement_descriptions.INT-006: HITL Decision Interface SHALL accept analyst decision objects containing action, rationale, actor, and role.
requirement_descriptions.INT-007: Re-Run Interface SHALL accept stage restart requests and resume execution from selected stage with preserved run context.
requirement_descriptions.INT-008: Visualization Interface SHALL provide read access to graph nodes, flows, boundaries, threats, mitigations, and evidence references.
requirement_descriptions.INT-009: Visualization Edit Interface SHALL submit proposed changes as typed patch operations rather than direct artifact overwrite.
requirement_descriptions.INT-010: STIX Export Interface SHALL output a standards-conformant STIX 2.1 bundle artifact with validation result metadata.
requirement_descriptions.INT-011: Report Export Interface SHALL output markdown report artifact and structured section index.
requirement_descriptions.INT-012: Provider Configuration Interface SHALL accept provider name, model name, mode, and policy profile settings.
requirement_descriptions.INT-013: Security Interface SHALL enforce role-based authorization checks before any edit, approve, or release action.
requirement_descriptions.INT-014: Audit Retrieval Interface SHALL return immutable change history for a selected run and artifact.
requirement_descriptions.INT-015: Model Connection Interface SHALL accept provider name, endpoint URL, API key, authentication method, model name, and deployment-specific parameters, and SHALL return a connection validation result indicating success, connectivity error, or authentication failure.
requirement_descriptions.SCR-013: INT-015|Model Connection Contract|Model Connection Interface SHALL accept provider name, endpoint URL, API key, authentication method, model name, and deployment-specific parameters, and SHALL return a connection validation result indicating success, connectivity error, or authentication failure.|Structured model configuration enables dynamic provider switching and integration with diverse LLM instances without code changes.|Test|Verified by connection tests with valid and invalid endpoints, confirming successful connection, clear error messages, model availability checks, and  API-key input handling for providers that require authentication.
requirement_descriptions.HITL-001: Threat Modeler SHALL provide Scope Confirmation Gate after context merge completion.
requirement_descriptions.HITL-002: Threat Modeler SHALL provide Trust Boundary Approval Gate after trust-boundary validation.
requirement_descriptions.HITL-003: Threat Modeler SHALL provide STRIDE Calibration Gate after STRIDE scoring.
requirement_descriptions.HITL-004: Threat Modeler SHALL provide Threat Plausibility Gate after threat generation.
requirement_descriptions.HITL-005: Threat Modeler SHALL provide Mitigation Adequacy Gate after mitigation generation.
requirement_descriptions.HITL-006: Threat Modeler SHALL provide Final Release Gate before report and STIX publication.
requirement_descriptions.HITL-007: Threat Modeler SHALL require rationale entry for analyst overrides at all gates.
requirement_descriptions.HITL-008: Threat Modeler SHALL preserve gate decisions as signed run records.
requirement_descriptions.HITL-009: Threat Modeler SHALL provide Input Integrity Gate before context merge to validate parsed ICD spreadsheets and narrative source documents.
requirement_descriptions.HITL-010: Threat Modeler SHALL provide a conditional Merge Conflict Resolution Gate after context merge when incoming data conflicts with approved baseline artifacts.
requirement_descriptions.HITL-011: Threat Modeler SHALL provide a conditional Export Consistency Gate before publication when canonical JSON, STIX, diagram, or report consistency checks fail or warning thresholds are exceeded.
requirement_descriptions.HITL-012: Orchestrator SHALL track and record for each conditional gate (HITL-010, HITL-011) whether the trigger condition was met (triggered=true) or not met (triggered=false) at the point the gate evaluation occurs. This state SHALL be persisted in the run result record.
requirement_descriptions.C02-A01-001: Agent 1 SHALL transform raw text and table inputs into canonical graph structures without introducing unsupported fields.
requirement_descriptions.C01-STATE-001: State Store SHALL version canonical graph snapshots per run and per stage.
requirement_descriptions.C01-ORCH-001: LangGraph Orchestrator SHALL route execution through all enabled agents using explicit next-state transitions.
requirement_descriptions.C01-ORCH-002: LangGraph Orchestrator SHALL persist checkpoints after each stage transition.
requirement_descriptions.C01-STATE-003: Validation Layer SHALL block stage handoff on schema failure and emit structured error records.
requirement_descriptions.C04-A03-001: Agent 3 SHALL evaluate each data flow for trust-boundary crossing status using configured policy rules.
requirement_descriptions.C05-A04-001: Agent 4 SHALL assign STRIDE severity scores for each data flow using the configured scoring scale.
requirement_descriptions.C06-A05-001: Agent 5 SHALL generate concrete threats for flows meeting configured risk trigger criteria.
requirement_descriptions.C07-A06-001: Agent 6 SHALL transform approved threat artifacts into a valid STIX 2.1 bundle.
requirement_descriptions.C08-A07-001: Agent 7 SHALL map each approved threat to technical and administrative controls based on configured control frameworks.
requirement_descriptions.C09-A08-001: Agent 8 SHALL generate Level 0, Level 1, and selected Level 2 Mermaid diagrams from canonical graph data.
requirement_descriptions.C10-A09-001: Agent 9 SHALL generate a formal markdown report containing executive summary, scope, boundaries, findings, mitigations, and residual risk sections.
requirement_descriptions.C12-HITL-001: The system SHALL implement HITL gates at all required decision points (input integrity, scope, boundary, STRIDE, threat, mitigation, release).
requirement_descriptions.C12-HITL-002: The system SHALL enforce role-based permissions for all HITL actions.
requirement_descriptions.C01-STATE-002: State Store SHALL preserve analyst-approved baselines as non-editable history entries.
requirement_descriptions.C12-HITL-003: The system SHALL record a complete audit trail for all HITL actions, including rationale and before/after state.
requirement_descriptions.C12-HITL-004: The system SHALL require rationale for all analyst overrides at gates.
requirement_descriptions.C11-LLM-001: Model Adapter SHALL select active model provider and model name from runtime configuration.
requirement_descriptions.C11-LLM-003: Model Adapter SHALL support future provider additions without agent contract changes.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-012: The GUI SHALL provide a model configuration screen that displays available model providers (local, hosted cloud services, commercial API services), allows analysts to select a provider, and presents provider-specific connection options without requiring source code changes. The configuration screen SHALL also include pipeline stage selection controls that allow analysts to enable or disable individual pipeline stages (agent_01 through agent_09) via checkbox controls, with validation requiring at least one stage to remain enabled.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-013: The GUI SHALL provide a configuration form for entering and editing model connection details including API endpoint, API key, authentication credentials, model name, deployment ID, and region-specific settings, with secure storage of sensitive credentials (encrypted or credential manager integration).
requirement_descriptions.GUI-014: The GUI SHALL provide a test-connection action that validates model connectivity and authentication before commencing a pipeline run, returning a user-readable status message and blocking run initiation if validation fails.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-015: The GUI SHALL provide a token usage screen that reports per-stage and aggregate token usage metrics (prompt, completion, reasoning, cached, total, request count) for live LLM runs, and SHALL provide export of token usage data as a run artifact for verification evidence.
requirement_descriptions.C11-LLM-002: Model Adapter SHALL support policy-constrained model allowlists by deployment mode.
requirement_descriptions.C06-A05-002: Agent 5 SHALL attach threat taxonomy references where available, including ATTACK, CAPEC, and CWE identifiers.
requirement_descriptions.C08-A07-003: Agent 7 SHALL include rationale linking control selections to threat mechanics.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-006: The GUI SHALL provide an export panel that allows analysts to download completed run outputs in canonical JSON, STIX 2.1 bundle, Mermaid diagram, and Markdown report formats.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-007: The GUI SHALL provide a snapshot export action that captures the complete run state, including inputs, all intermediate stage results, HITL decisions, prompt configuration, and run metadata, into a single portable file.
requirement_descriptions.C03-A02-001: Agent 2 SHALL merge new submissions into existing canonical graphs without deleting existing approved elements.
requirement_descriptions.C09-A08-003: Agent 8 SHALL preserve deterministic node and edge identifiers across regenerations for unchanged structures.
requirement_descriptions.C04-A03-002: Agent 3 SHALL emit trust-boundary review flags for human approval when confidence is below policy threshold.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-001: The GUI SHALL provide a form-based input screen for analyst entry of system name, description, data flows, assets, trust boundaries, and deployment context prior to pipeline execution.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-002: The GUI SHALL provide a dedicated screen for each HITL gate that presents the relevant stage outputs, supports approve, edit, and override actions, and captures rationale for all non-approve decisions.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-002B: The GUI SHALL execute HITL gate resume actions in a non-blocking background thread so that the Streamlit UI thread is not blocked during resumed pipeline execution. The run registry status SHALL transition to RUNNING while resumption is in progress, and the pipeline status dashboard SHALL display live stage progress updates during resumed execution in the same manner as the initial run.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-003: The GUI SHALL provide a pipeline status view that displays the current executing stage, completed stages, pending stages, and any blocking conditions in real time during execution.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-003B: Every GUI screen SHALL synchronize pipeline execution state from the process-level run registry at the start of each render pass before displaying screen content. This synchronization SHALL apply to all screens including but not limited to: Home dashboard, Stage Results, Threat Review, Results Export, and Snapshot Manager.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-003C: All GUI screens that display run artifacts (Results Export, Snapshot Manager, Threat Review, Stage Results) SHALL present state consistent with the most recently completed or in-progress background execution and SHALL NOT display stale pre-run or pre-resume state when a completed or in-progress run exists in the run registry.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-004: The GUI SHALL provide a results viewer for each pipeline stage that renders the stage output artifacts and makes them accessible to the analyst before and after HITL review.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-005: The GUI SHALL provide a threat review subview within the Artifacts section that renders scored threats alongside their mapped mitigations and supports inline approval and edit actions per threat record.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-011: The GUI SHALL enforce role-based access controls consistent with INT-013 such that edit, approve, override, export, snapshot, and agent prompt-edit actions are restricted to authorized roles and unauthorized actions are blocked at the GUI layer.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-030: The GUI SHALL display all defined HITL gates in pipeline order on the HITL GATES page, and SHALL summarize gate lifecycle counts for Approved, Rejected, Bypassed, and Pending states without splitting the workflow into separate status-only sections.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-031: The GUI SHALL keep execution timeline visibility in the global footer, SHALL render centered plain-language status text for the current run state (for example, Running Input Normalizer or Paused for Input Integrity Gate), and SHALL allow operators to remain on the HITL GATES page while the run continues or resumes. The GUI SHALL not expose an execution-only operator path in the primary shell.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-032: The GUI SHALL enforce review of a preflight Input Integrity gate before Stage 1 execution proceeds, SHALL present parsed input intent and integrity checks in human-readable form (including source presence, text and table summaries), and SHALL require explicit approve or reject decisions with analyst rationale.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-033: The GUI SHALL enforce a dedicated normalization review gate immediately after Stage 1 and before Stage 2, SHALL render a human-readable summary of normalized canonical graph content (system, counts, interfaces, and validation checks), and SHALL block Stage 2 execution until approve or reject decision is submitted.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-041: The GUI SHALL treat the header control rows as the authoritative artifact-domain navigation surface for Canonical Graph, Trust Boundaries, STRIDE Viewer, Threats, Mermaid Diagrams, STIX Bundle, and Report. The persistent left rail SHALL remain visible and SHALL be limited to global application and run/workspace controls rather than duplicate artifact-domain switching.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-042: The GUI SHALL provide explicit icon-labeled header navigation entries for Threat Review and Results Export within the main control strip. The Results Export action SHALL be reachable from both the header and the persistent left menu, and SHALL expose mitigations export actions through the export surface.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-008: The GUI SHALL provide a snapshot restore action that imports a previously exported snapshot file and reconstitutes the run state so that the analyst can continue analysis, review history, or audit the prior run.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-009: The GUI SHALL provide an agent configuration screen that displays the current active prompt for each pipeline agent and allows authorized users to edit and save updated prompts without requiring source code changes.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-010: The GUI SHALL maintain a version history of saved agent prompts and allow authorized users to view prior prompt versions and revert to a selected prior version.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-016: The GUI SHALL render execution status, provider mode, and gate/stage progress from backend asynchronous runtime-state projections and SHALL NOT rely on screen-local session state as authoritative runtime state.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-017: If a run configured for live LLM mode degrades to fixture/offline mode, the GUI SHALL display a hard failure status and explicit fallback reason, and SHALL report execution as halted.
requirement_descriptions.C01-ORCH-003: Pipeline configuration SHALL support both `linear` and `langgraph-compatible` execution modes. Release and validation profiles SHALL use `langgraph-compatible`, while `linear` mode SHALL be treated as a compatibility mode for controlled scenarios.
requirement_descriptions.VS-009: Sprint Team SHALL maintain at least one automated visible-browser validation scenario that exercises UI file upload behavior with approved sprint fixtures (including markdown narratives) and records command + fixture evidence in sprint test documentation.
requirement_descriptions.C01-ORCH-005: Orchestrator SHALL pass each approved stage output to the next enabled agent as a canonical handoff record that preserves correlation identifier, source stage, compliance metadata, and approved version reference.
requirement_descriptions.C02-A01-004: Agent 1 SHALL preserve source provenance for ICD spreadsheet rows and narrative documents and SHALL emit structured compliance flags when required fields, interface references, or source mappings are missing or inconsistent.
requirement_descriptions.C03-A02-003: Agent 2 SHALL preserve the input-compliance and provenance metadata produced by Agent 1 and SHALL emit a structured validation failure when upstream ICD compliance data is missing, stale, or contradictory.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-001A: The GUI SHALL automatically invoke the threat modeling pipeline (all 9 agents) immediately upon successful form submission and file validation, without requiring an additional explicit "Start Pipeline" button or user action.
requirement_descriptions.C01-ORCH-004: Orchestrator SHALL pause execution at each HITL gate, persist the gate context and decision state, and resume only after an explicit approved decision is recorded.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-003A: When execution is paused by a HITL gate, the GUI SHALL display the gate identifier, gate status, and count of completed stages, and SHALL not present the paused state as a runtime failure.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-012A: The GUI SHALL display all 9 pipeline stages (agent_01 through agent_09) with human-readable labels and individual checkbox controls for enabling/disabling each stage. At least one stage must remain enabled at all times. Stage selection changes SHALL persist after clicking Apply Settings and SHALL be recovered on subsequent visits to the configuration screen.
requirement_descriptions.ADM-001: Project Management Process SHALL require each feature branch to reference a planning issue before development starts.
requirement_descriptions.ADM-002: Pull Request Process SHALL require each feature pull request to reference at least one tracked issue and update issue status on merge.
requirement_descriptions.ADM-003: Release Process SHALL require a completed feature branch checklist before pull request approval.
requirement_descriptions.ADM-004: Feature Branch Workflow SHALL store completed checklist artifacts for each merged feature branch.
requirement_descriptions.ADM-005: Release Management Process SHALL conduct release readiness review using aggregated branch checklist evidence.
requirement_descriptions.ADM-006: Project Governance Process SHALL schedule recurring backlog, branch, and release sync reviews at defined cadence.
requirement_descriptions.VS-001: Requirement Owner SHALL assign at least one verification method to each requirement ID.
requirement_descriptions.VS-002: Requirement Owner SHALL define objective pass criteria for each requirement ID.
requirement_descriptions.VS-003: Test Team SHALL map automated tests to requirement IDs for all schema, orchestration, and interface contracts.
requirement_descriptions.VS-004: Review Team SHALL perform inspection-based verification for HITL workflow and audit controls.
requirement_descriptions.VS-005: Integration Team SHALL perform end-to-end demonstration of a complete run with approvals and exports.
requirement_descriptions.VS-006: Sprint Team SHALL record demonstration evidence (annotated screenshots or screen recording) for every sprint that delivers runnable user-facing functionality. Evidence SHALL be attached to the sprint PR and referenced in the sprint test execution summary.
requirement_descriptions.VS-007: Sprint demonstration SHALL cover, at minimum, the user-facing deliverables of that sprint: pipeline execution for pipeline sprints; HITL gate pause and resume for HITL sprints; screen walkthrough for HMI sprints; full end-to-end run from input to export for release sprints.
requirement_descriptions.VS-008: For release-candidate sprints that intentionally exclude automation from release gating, Sprint Team SHALL execute and document a full manual release-candidate validation campaign that includes functional workflow checks and documentation walkthrough checks (user manual, product documentation set, and deployment guide).
requirement_descriptions.VS-010: For runtime state transitions and HITL gate publication paths, Sprint Team SHALL execute a race-condition verification control that checks causal ordering invariants (for example, Gate 0 payload-ready-before-paused projection) using automated API tests and at least one timestamped polling probe, and SHALL record evidence in sprint governance artifacts.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-002A: The GUI SHALL render gate-review artifacts in human-readable summaries in addition to raw structured payloads, including counts, labels, subsystem or interface names, and concise automated checks relevant to the gate under review.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-018: The GUI SHALL provide a dedicated STIX viewer that renders the generated STIX 2.1 bundle with object grouping (attack-pattern, course-of-action, relationship) and basic search/filter controls for analyst review.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-019: The GUI SHALL provide a dedicated canonical graph viewer that renders system, subsystem, component, function, and interface structures from the canonical graph artifact in a navigable hierarchical layout.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-020: The GUI SHALL provide an in-app Mermaid diagram viewer for generated Level 0/1/2 diagram content with source-text toggle and render error visibility.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-021: The GUI SHALL provide a dedicated STRIDE threat model viewer that presents per-interface STRIDE scores, justifications, and associated threats in sortable tabular form.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-022: The GUI SHALL provide an explicit export action for STRIDE threat model results as a standalone artifact (JSON or CSV) in addition to existing full-run exports.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-023: The Results Export quick preview controls SHALL expand and render artifact previews for canonical graph, STIX bundle, report, Mermaid diagrams, and token usage in the active run context.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-024: The GUI SHALL display release-governed component semantic versions and component-file version identifiers in Results Export and Snapshot Manager views, and SHALL provide export of the same version inventories as release evidence artifacts.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-025: The GUI SHALL provide a markdown viewer and editor to open, preview, edit, and save markdown files generated or managed by the tool, with clear save-state feedback and basic edit safeguards.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-026: The GUI SHALL display live heartbeat age and the configured timeout threshold on execution status surfaces and SHALL surface backend stall failures with actionable messaging.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-027: The GUI SHALL provide a dedicated Run Diagnostics panel that shows status, elapsed time, run ID, stage, gate, provider, and heartbeat age in one view.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-028: The GUI SHALL decode execution errors for readability, surface provider HTTP status codes when available, and provide the raw error payload in a copyable form for diagnostics.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-029: The GUI SHALL correlate prompt text and model response by prompt record identifier on the Last Prompt screen, display only the response matching the selected prompt, and suppress stale responses from prior attempts.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-034: The GUI SHALL parse Mermaid artifact payloads into a selectable diagram list, SHALL show the selected diagram in rendered and source-editable forms with toggleable split/diagram/text display modes, and SHALL display a position indicator with selection name (`x of n - diagram name`).
requirement_descriptions.GUI-035: The GUI SHALL keep the primary navigation rail visible at all times on the main HMI shell and SHALL NOT expose a menu button that collapses or hides the rail during normal operation.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-036: The GUI SHALL render a top-of-content control strip that mirrors the primary operator workflow sections used most often during monitoring, excluding artifact browsing because artifact selection is always available inside the artifact viewer.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-037: When a run is created through the setup wizard, the GUI SHALL auto-select that exact run ID, SHALL avoid auto-selecting an unrelated run during the initial refresh window, and SHALL display a temporary `Created by wizard` badge on the pinned run row for 30 seconds.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-043: The GUI SHALL render a narrow, unlabeled parsing segment immediately before every gate boundary in the execution timeline, including Gate 0. The segment SHALL display brown while parsing is in progress and green when parsing is complete. The visualization SHALL align with backend readiness-coupled gate opening behavior so operators can distinguish parse-in-progress from gate-ready states.
requirement_descriptions.RHMI-009: API integration test + UI functional test
requirement_descriptions.RHMI-010: Component behavior validation + browser workflow test
requirement_descriptions.RHMI-018: Component behavior validation + API integration test
requirement_descriptions.RHMI-019: Contract validation test + release checklist inspection
requirement_descriptions.RIC-001: The orchestrator SHALL NOT open Gate 0 until preflight input integrity data is present and minimally complete for gate review payload construction. If readiness is not achieved within the configured wait window, execution SHALL fail with an explicit readiness timeout error.
requirement_descriptions.RIC-002: The runtime run manager SHALL treat user cancellation as a first-class terminal CANCELLED status for active and paused runs, SHALL clear pause metadata at cancellation time, and SHALL prevent paused overlays from superseding terminal status in API/UI projections.
requirement_descriptions.RIC-003: Frontend submission preprocessing SHALL preserve parse parity with backend expectations by placing parsed table data into structured state and excluding raw binary spreadsheet payloads from free-text fields.
requirement_descriptions.RIC-004: Prompt expected-output declarations SHALL remain aligned with enforced JSON/schema contracts; mismatch conditions SHALL be detected by validation and surfaced as actionable defects before release sign-off.
requirement_descriptions.RIC-005: Runtime state publication SHALL enforce a deterministic ordering invariant for Gate 0: paused status and pause_gate metadata SHALL NOT be externally projected until the corresponding Gate 0 preflight artifact payload is present in checkpoint-backed gate state. This invariant SHALL be treated as an architecture contract and SHALL be enforced by API projection and run-lifecycle tests.
requirement_descriptions.PRM-001: Keeps behavior instructions decoupled from format exemplars.
requirement_descriptions.PRM-002: Prevents runtime/editor drift and inconsistent behavior across all execution contexts.
requirement_descriptions.PRM-003: Ensures minimum behavioral verbosity and operator-auditable scope.
requirement_descriptions.PRM-004: Avoids under-specified prompts that degrade behavior determinism.
requirement_descriptions.PRM-005: Protects schema continuity and prevents partial-shape regressions.
requirement_descriptions.PRM-S01: Consistent authoring model improves maintainability and review quality.
requirement_descriptions.PRM-S02: Reduces prompt bloat and lowers change-coupling between behavior and examples.
requirement_descriptions.PRM-S03: Improves resilience under partial or low-confidence model outputs.
requirement_descriptions.PRM-S04: Supports safe evolution and audit traceability.
requirement_descriptions.GUI-040: Dual-surface threat artifact and mitigation-review viewer capability.
requirement_descriptions.HITL-00X: Legacy placeholder HITL gate requirement identifier retained for tracker compatibility until normalized ID replacement is approved.
requirement_descriptions.C11-LLM-004: The system SHALL apply a configurable timeout and retry budget to live LLM requests, and the default live profile SHALL use a 900 second timeout and 2 attempts unless a higher-level policy overrides those values.
requirement_descriptions.C02-A01-002: Agent 1 SHALL assign deterministic identifiers to new systems, subsystems, components, and data flows.
requirement_descriptions.C02-A01-003: Agent 1 SHALL mark unknown trust-boundary status explicitly when source data is insufficient.
requirement_descriptions.C03-A02-002: Agent 2 SHALL record merge-conflict notes for analyst review when contradictory source claims are detected.
requirement_descriptions.C05-A04-002: Agent 4 SHALL provide concise justification text for each STRIDE dimension score.
requirement_descriptions.C05-A04-003: Agent 4 SHALL preserve analyst-overridden scores and associated rationale metadata.
requirement_descriptions.C06-A05-003: Agent 5 SHALL emit likelihood and impact values for each generated threat.
requirement_descriptions.C07-A06-002: Agent 6 SHALL include stable object identifiers and relationship links for generated STIX entities.
requirement_descriptions.C08-A07-004: Agent 7 SHALL store mitigations_technical and mitigations_administrative arrays under each threat object in canonical graph output.
requirement_descriptions.C08-A07-002: Agent 7 SHALL assign residual-risk estimates after proposed controls.
requirement_descriptions.C09-A08-002: Agent 8 SHALL render trust boundaries and risk severity overlays using configured visual conventions.
requirement_descriptions.C10-A09-002: Agent 9 SHALL reference approved diagrams, threats, and controls from current run artifacts only.
requirement_descriptions.C10-A09-003: Agent 9 SHALL produce report outputs suitable for downstream document conversion workflows.
requirement_descriptions.C12-HITL-005: The system SHALL evaluate configured trigger rules for conditional Merge Conflict Resolution and Export Consistency gates.
requirement_descriptions.C12-HITL-006: Audit Service SHALL capture analyst decision records for Gate 0 input integrity review before context merge.
requirement_descriptions.HITL-013: Conditional gate state in the run record SHALL have one of three explicit values: (1) "Open" when condition is triggered and gate is awaiting analyst decision, (2) "Auto-Bypassed" when condition is not met and gate automatically closes, (3) "Rejected" or "Accepted" after analyst decision. The dashboard SHALL NOT report "Pending" for gates that are auto-bypassed.
requirement_descriptions.HITL-014: The Run Dashboard HITL Gate States table SHALL display conditional gates with status "🟢 Auto-Bypassed" (distinct emoji) when the gate's trigger condition is not met, and SHALL display mandatory gates and triggered conditional gates with status "❓ Open" or "✅ Accepted" or "❌ Rejected" as appropriate.
requirement_descriptions.HITL-015: Conditional gate record in the run result SHALL include trigger_condition_met (boolean) and trigger_reason (string) fields documenting which specific threshold or condition was evaluated and whether it was satisfied.
